title: One vehicle access point per lot (R40 and above)
text: In areas R40 and above, vehicle access points are limited to one per lot (refer Figure 3.7a) except where: i. an existing dwelling is being retained that has an established access point that is not able to serve the other dwellings; ii. dwellings front the street and access is not available from a communal street or rear right-of-way; or iii. the lot frontage exceeds 40m, two vehicle access points are permitted.

exceptions.label: (i) retained dwelling with an established access point
(ii) dwellings front the street and no communal street or rear ROW access
(iii) lot frontage exceeds 40 m: two access points

replaces.note: Part C limit applied to grouped and multiple dwellings at R30+; Part B had no limit; new for single houses at R40+

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 2 - Single Houses.pdf

notes: Exception (i): 'not able to serve the other dwellings' is not tested (single house). Exception (ii) as printed states no limit; the register reads it as 'one per dwelling' (Part C wording) which the draft text does not say. 'Dwellings front the street' is not tested. R30-R35 are not covered (Part C had R30+ for grouped dwellings). LDPs and LPPs may vary C3.7.2 without WAPC approval.

verified.note: Wording, R40 and above coding and the 40m / two access points limb confirmed. Exceptions (i) and (ii) state no effect and are written for several dwellings ('serve the other dwellings', 'dwellings front the street'); how they apply to a single house is not stated on the page. Encoded as not applicable.
